q: Calculate the change in volume for air and for dry sand.
Use particles to explain the results for air and water.
Air particles are far apart with lots of free space, so they can be pushed closer. Water particles are already touching, so the volume does not change.
Dry sand squashed a little but wet sand did not. Explain this difference.
In dry sand the spaces between grains are full of air, which squashes. In wet sand the spaces are filled with water, which cannot be squashed, so the volume stays the same.
